info.title: Khalid API
info.description: The Content API and the Admin API of a Khalid blog.

post.summary:
Creates a draft post from markdown, or from HTML with `source=html`. A
retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the post the first
request made, so it never makes two (RULES.md BL-API-7). Needs
`posts:write`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `html` to send the body as HTML; markdown otherwise.

schema.description: What a new post's body is written in.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Any text up to 255 characters that names this request, so a retry makes no second post

parameters.name: Accept-Version
parameters.description: The oldest API version the client accepts, such as v1.0.

400.description: The source is neither markdown nor html

401.description: No valid integration key or staff token

422.description: The body could not be read

get.summary: Reads one post in any status. Needs `posts:write`.

parameters.name: Accept-Version
parameters.description: The oldest API version the client accepts, such as v1.0.

401.description: No valid integration key or staff token

404.description: No post has this identity

put.summary:
Edits one post, and publishes it with `"status": "published"` once
the linter lets it through, or with `"status": "scheduled"` and a
future `published_at` at that time. The edit carries the `updated_at` of the copy it was
made on; when the post changed since, the answer is a 409 naming who
changed it and when (RULES.md BL-API-7). Needs `posts:write`.

parameters.name: Accept-Version
parameters.description: The oldest API version the client accepts, such as v1.0.

401.description: No valid integration key or staff token

404.description: No post has this identity

409.description: The post changed after the copy the edit was made on

422.description: The body could not be read, the schedule cannot be kept, or the linter refused to publish the post

AdminPost.description:
A post in Admin API shape: any status, with its markdown source and
the `updated_at` an edit must send back (RULES.md BL-API-7).

author.description: The author's slug, matching a file in the site's `authors/` folder.

markdown.description: The markdown source, which the content file holds.

published_at.description: When it went or goes live; empty for a draft.

slug.description: The last part of its address.

unpublish_at.description: When it comes down again, if it is scheduled to.

updated_at.description: When it last changed. An edit sends this back unchanged.

updated_by.description: Who made the last change: a staff name or a key's identity.

AdminPosts.description: Posts as the Admin API wraps them.

Author.description: An author in one language, in API shape.

bio.description: The introduction from the author's file, in markdown.

id.description: The language and the slug, such as `en.asif`.

role.description: What the author does, such as `Founder of SerpDad`.

same_as.description: The author's profiles elsewhere, in the order the file gives them.

slug.description: The slug posts name the author by.

url.description: The author's page on the blog, when it has one.

authors.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

Bodies.description: A post's body in each format. A format left out of `formats` is absent.

case_studies.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

categories.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

changelog.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

collections.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

ContentCollection.description:
A collection in one language, in API shape: the folder's name and the
title and description its `_index.md` gives, when it has one.

description.description: The summary of its list page.

id.description: The language and the folder, such as `en.posts`.

slug.description: The folder's name, such as `posts` or `case-studies`.

title.description: The heading of its list page.

EditPosts.description: An edit, wrapped the way the Admin API wraps posts: exactly one.

glossary.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

Menu.description:
One menu in one language, in API shape, such as the header menu
`primary` or the `footer` menu. An empty menu shows nothing.

id.description: The language and the menu, such as `en.primary`.

links.description: The links, in the order readers see them.

url.description:
Where it goes: a path on the site, such as `/blog/about/`, or a full
address.

navigation.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

NewPost.description: A new post as a client sends it, before any checks.

author.description:
The author's slug, such as `asif`. The linter refuses to publish a
post without one.

slug.description: The slug; made from the title when left out.

NewPosts.description: A new post, wrapped the way the Admin API wraps posts: exactly one.

pages.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

Pagination.description: Where a page sits in its list, in Ghost's shape.

next.description: The next page, if there is one.

pages.description: How many pages the list has, at least 1.

prev.description: The previous page, if there is one.

total.description: How many items the list has.

allOf.description: The body, in the formats asked for.

authors.description: Author slugs, in the order the writer gave them.

excerpt.description: A short summary, if the writer gave one.

featured.description: Whether the post is marked as featured.

id.description: Stable across edits: the content file's identity.

slug.description: The last part of its address.

tags.description: Tag slugs, in the order the writer gave them.

Post.description:
A published post in API shape. Bodies are present only when asked for
with `formats`.

PostEdit.description:
An edit to a post: the fields to change, and the `updated_at` of the
copy it was made on. Fields left out keep their value. A `status` of
`published` publishes a draft, once the linter lets it through;
`scheduled` with a future `published_at` publishes it then, and
`draft` takes a scheduled post off its schedule.

published_at.description:
When a `scheduled` post goes live: a time to come, with its offset,
such as `2026-11-03T09:00:00+01:00`.

status.description:
`published` to publish the post now, `scheduled` to publish it at
`published_at`, or `draft` to cancel a schedule. Publishing runs
the linter, and a post with a blocking finding stays a draft.

unpublish_at.description:
When the post comes down again: a time to come, after
`published_at` for a scheduled post.

updated_at.description: The `updated_at` of the copy the edit was made on.

posts.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

Problem.description:
An error as the API sends it (RULES.md BL-ERR-5): `type`, `title`,
`status` and `detail`, plus `fix`, and `rule` and `instance` where they
apply. `detail` and `fix` come from a [`UserMessage`], so they say what
happened, why it matters and what to do (BL-ERR-4).

detail.description: What happened and why it matters.

instance.description: The address the problem is about.

lint.description:
For a post the linter refused, every finding, as `khalid lint
--json` prints them.

rule.description: The lint rule or parameter that produced the problem.

title.description: The same short title for every problem of this kind.

type.description: A link to the page that explains this kind of problem.

Settings.description:
The public settings of the site, in API shape: its name, where it lives
and its languages. Nothing secret is ever part of it.

default_language.description: The language a reader gets first, such as `en`.

languages.description: Every language the site is written in, the default among them.

url.description: The address of the blog's front page in the default language.

SiteSettings.description: The site's settings, as every response wraps them: a list of one.

tags.description: The entries on this page, or the one entry asked for.

Term.description:
A tag or a category in one language, in API shape. Both are a name for
a group of posts, so they share one shape.

id.description: The language and the slug, such as `en.on-page-seo`.

name.description: The name readers see in this language.

slug.description: The slug posts name it by.

admin_key.name: Authorization
admin_key.description: An integration key or staff token, as Khalid followed by the key.

content_key.name: Authorization
content_key.description: The site's content key, as Khalid-Content followed by the key.
